thought.text: One leftover process (PID 1520). Let me kill it specifically and clean up temp files:

reasoning_content: Port 8080 is no longer listening, but the process `node /tmp/serve.js` (PID 1520) still exists — it might be in the middle of shutting down, or the listener may have closed but the process is hanging around. Wait, port 8080 is shown as not listening, yet the process is still alive? Weird. Let me kill that specific PID and clean up the files. Actually, maybe ss's output was just stale. Either way, I'll kill PID 1520 individually.

action.command: kill 1520 2>/dev/null; sleep 1; ps -p 1520 > /dev/null 2>&1 && echo "1520 still alive" || echo "1520 gone"; rm -f /tmp/serve.js /tmp/dev.log /tmp/static.log /tmp/page.html /tmp/sp.html; ls /tmp/serve.js 2>&1; (ss -tlnp 2>/dev/null) | grep -E ':3000|:8080' || echo "ports clear"
